Rashi on Sukkah 14a:10:1.english: One may roof with boards - In the Gemara, [it] explains their dispute.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:10:2.english: If one placed a board that is four [handbreadths] wide upon it - In the Gemara, it explains who taught this.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:10:3.hebrew: ובלבד שלא יישן תחתיו - דנסר רחב ד' סכך פסול הוא, כדאמר בגמרא: לרב אליבא דר' מאיר, ולשמואל לדברי הכל. וסוכה כשרה — וכגון דיהביה אצל הדופן, דסכך פסול אינו פוסל מן הצד אלא בד' אמות, דאמרינן דופן עקומה:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:10:3.english: Provided he does not sleep beneath it - For a board four [handbreadths] wide is invalid roofing, as [the Gemara] says in the Gemara: according to Rav, in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi Meir; and according to Shmuel, according to everyone. And [as for the ruling that the] sukkah is fit — [this is in a case] such as where he placed it next to the wall, for invalid roofing does not invalidate [a sukkah] from the side unless [it is] four cubits, as we say [the principle of] curved wall [dofen akumah].

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:11:1.english: The dispute is with regard to boards that have four [handbreadths] - For most house ceilings are made of them.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:11:2.hebrew: ר' מאיר - דפסיל, אית ליה גזרת תקרה: אי מכשרת בהו, אתי למימר: "מה לי לסכך באלו, מה לי לישב תחת קורות ביתי? אף היא בנסרים מקורה!" וההוא ודאי פסול, דסוכה אמר רחמנא, ולא ביתו של כל ימות השנה:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:11:2.english: Rabbi Meir - [The reason] that he invalidates [them is that] he holds [there is] a decree of the ceiling: If you validate [roofing] with them, one will come to say, "What difference is there to me whether I roof with these or whether I sit beneath the beams of my house? It, too, is roofed with boards!" And that is certainly invalid, for the Merciful One said [to dwell in a] "sukkah," and not in one's year-round house.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:11:3.hebrew: אבל בנסרים שאין בהם ד' - שאין רוב תקרות עשויות מהן:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:11:3.english: However, with regard to boards that do not have four handbreadths - For most ceilings are not made from them.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:11:4.english: Everyone agrees [that the sukkah is] fit - For [they] do not resemble a ceiling, that [the Sages] should issue a decree concerning them.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:11:5.hebrew: בשאין בהן ד' מחלוקת - בההוא מכשר ר' יהודה, משום דאין רוב תקרות עשויות מהן — לא גזרינן בהו. ור' מאיר חייש למיעוט, שיש מיעוט העושין תקרה מהן:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:11:5.english: The dispute is with regard to [boards] that do not have four [handbreadths] in them - In that [case], Rabbi Yehuda deems [it] fit: Since most ceilings are not made from them, we do not issue a decree concerning them. And Rabbi Meir is concerned for the minority, as there is a minority who make a ceiling from them.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:12:1.hebrew: אין בהן ארבעה - קפסיל ר' מאיר:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:12:1.english: [When] they do not have four - Rabbi Meir disqualifies [them].

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:12:2.english: Even with [boards] less than three [handbreadths] - [This is said] in astonishment:

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:12:3.hebrew: הא קנים בעלמא נינהו - וא"כ, במאי מכשר:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:12:3.english: Aren’t they merely reeds - And if so, with what does [Rabbi Meir] validate [a sukkah]?

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:13:1.hebrew: א"ר פפא הכי קאמר - שמואל: יש בהן ארבעה — דברי הכל פסולה, כו':
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:13:1.english: Rav Pappa said: This is what he is saying - Shmuel [is saying]: If they have four [handbreadths], everyone agrees [that it is] unfit, etc.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:13:2.english: The measure of a place - For there is no domain in less than four [handbreadths].

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:13:3.hebrew: לא גזרינן - משום תקרה, דלא חשיבי לעשות תקרה מהן:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:13:3.english: We do not issue a decree - On account of a ceiling, as they are not significant [enough] to make a ceiling from them.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:13:4.hebrew: כיון דנפקי מתורת לבוד - שאם היה אויר במקום אחד מהם, לא מצי למימר לבוד — חשיבי להיות דומות לתקרה, וגזרי':
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:13:4.english: Since they have departed from the status of lavud - For if there were an airspace in place of one of them, one could not say [that it is] lavud — [therefore,] they are significant [enough] to resemble a ceiling, and we decree [against using them].

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:14:1.hebrew: תנן נתן עליה נסר כו' - קא סלקא דעתיה: דברי הכל היא; וכשרה — וכגון שנתנו מן הצד, דאמרינן דופן עקומה, ולא חשיב סכך למיפסלה:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:14:1.english: We learned: If one placed a board atop it, etc. - [The Gemara] presumed that [the Mishnah] is [the opinion of] all; and [as for the ruling that it is] fit — [it is in a case] such as where he placed it at the side, for we say [the principle of] curved wall [dofen akumah], and it is not considered s'chach [so as] to invalidate it.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:16:1.hebrew: שני סדינין מצטרפין - לארבעה טפחים לפסול בסוכה, משום סכך פסול שסיכך בדבר המקבל טומאה; וסכך פסול באמצע פוסל בארבעה:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:16:1.english: Two sheets join together - To four handbreadths to disqualify [the sukkah] on account of unfit roofing, since he roofed with an object susceptible to ritual impurity; and unfit roofing in the middle invalidates at four [handbreadths].

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:1:1.hebrew: יורדין לידי טומאה במחשבה - מי שחשב עליו שזה יהא גמר מלאכתן, כגון שעיבדו לדרגש או לדולבקי, כיון שעיבדו, מקבל טומאה. ואלמלי עיבדו לרצועות וסנדלין, אין מקבלים טומאה עד שיגמרו למלאכת הסנדלין:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:1:1.english: [Vessels] descend into ritual impurity through thought - [In the case of] one who intended regarding it that this should be the completion of its manufacture, such as where he tanned it for a dargash [couch] or for a dulebki [table] — once he has tanned it, it becomes susceptible to ritual impurity. Whereas had he tanned it for straps and sandals, they do not become susceptible to ritual impurity until they are completed for the work of the sandals.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:1:2.hebrew: ואין עולים מטומאתן - ממחשבת תורת קבלת טומאה, אין עולין במחשבה. כגון: עיבדו לשלחן ולדרגש, וחישב עליו לרצועות וסנדלין — אין מחשבתו מבטלתן מתורת קבלת טומאה:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:1:2.english: And they do not ascend from their ritual impurity - From the thought that [imparted] the status of susceptibility to ritual impurity, they do not ascend through thought. For example, [if] he processed [a hide] for a table or for a couch, and [then] intended it for straps and sandals, his thought does not remove them from the status of susceptibility to ritual impurity.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:1:3.english: Only through a change resulting from an action - Until he applies a chisel to it.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:1:4.hebrew: מעשה מבטל מידי מעשה - אפילו עשה בו מעשה מוכיח מתחילה לשלחן, כגון שקיצצו סביבותיו ליפותו, כיון שנתן איזמל בו לחתכו לסנדלין, מבטל מעשה ראשון, וכל שכן שמוציא מידי מחשבה שלא היה בה מעשה:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:1:4.english: An action nullifies [the status created by] an action - Even if he performed on it an action that clearly demonstrates [its purpose] initially for a table [covering], such as where he trimmed around its edges to beautify it, once he applied a blade to it to cut it for sandals, [this] nullifies the first action; and all the more so does it negate [the status created by] thought, in which there was no action.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:2:1.hebrew: וכי תימא הני מילי - דלא מבטלין בתרייתא לקמייתא בכלים דחשיבי, ומשיצא עליו שם כלי במחשבה, אינה נוחה להפקיע שמה:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:2:1.english: And if you say this applies only - That a subsequent [thought] does not negate an earlier [thought] [applies only] to vessels, which are significant, and once the designation of a vessel has taken effect upon it through thought, it [the subsequent thought] is not readily able to revoke its designation.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:2:2.english: That one besasan - Below, [the Gemara] explains what it is.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:2:3.hebrew: טהורות - דגלי דעתיה דלא ניחא ליה בהו, וטהרו מלקבל טומאה הידות האלה עוד, ולא הביאה טומאה על האוכל עד שיגיע טומאה באוכל עצמו:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:2:3.english: [Are] ritually pure - For he revealed his intention that he has no use for them, and these handles have become pure from receiving ritual impurity any longer, nor do they bring ritual impurity upon the food until ritual impurity touches the food itself.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:2:4.hebrew: ור' יוסי מטמא - טעמא מפרש לקמן:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:2:4.english: And Rabbi Yosei deems [them] ritually impure - The reason is explained below.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:3:1.hebrew: בשלמא למאן דאמר - האי "בססן" היינו שהתיר אגדן של עומרין, לשון "מתבוססת בדמיך" (יחזקאל ט״ז:ו׳) — מתגוללת; כלומר: כיון שהתיר אגדן, השבלין מתגוללין בגורן, לפי שנוחין להתפזר. או לשון כנה, דמתרגמינן "ואת כנו" — "וית בסיסיה" (שמות ל), כלומר: הכנו לדשן:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:3:1.english: Granted, according to the one who said - This [word] besasan means that he untied the binding of the sheaves. [It is] in the sense of "wallowing [mitboseset] in your blood" (Ezekiel 16:6) — rolling about; that is to say, once he untied their binding, the stalks roll around on the threshing floor, because they easily scatter. Or, [it is] an expression of a base [kannah], as we translate [in Aramaic], "and its base" [ve-et kanno] — "and its base" [ve-yat basiseih] (Exodus 30); that is to say, he prepared it for threshing.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:3:2.hebrew: שפיר - לא קשיא לך, דאליביה מצית למימר דקיימי רבנן כוותיה, כיון שהתיר אגדן — דלא הוי אלא כמחשבה בעלמא — דגלי דעתיה דלא ניחא ליה בידות שלהן, שאין הידות ראויות לשבלין אלא כדי לאוגדן בהם, והאי מוכח דלא בעי לאוגדן:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:3:2.english: [It works out] well - It is not difficult for you, for according to him you can say that the Rabbis hold in accordance with his [view], since he untied their binding — which is nothing more than mere thought — as he revealed his intention that he has no use for their handles, for handles are suitable for stalks only in order to bind them with them, and this proves that he does not want to bind them.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:3:3.hebrew: אלא למאן דאמר בססן ממש - שדשן לידות ברגלי בהמה או במקבת, כמו: "בשמך נבוס קמינו" (תהילים מ״ד:ו׳), "בוססו את חלקתי" (ירמיהו י״ב:י׳). והכא דאיכא מעשה רבה — הוא דאמר דקא מטהרי רבנן, אבל במחשבה לא אמר:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:3:3.english: However, according to the one who said [that it means] he actually trampled them - That he threshed the handles with the feet of an animal or with a mallet, as in: “Through Your Name we will trample our adversaries” (Psalms 44:6), [and] “They have trampled My portion” (Jeremiah 12:10). And [only] here, where there is a substantial action, did he say that the Rabbis deem [them] ritually pure; but with [mere] thought, he did not say [so].

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:3:4.hebrew: מאי איכא למימר - אי בקוצר לאכילה מוקמת לה לההיא דלעיל, מאי טעמא דרבנן:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:3:4.english: What can be said? - If you establish that [baraita] above as [referring to one who] harvested for food, what is the rationale of the Rabbis?

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:4:1.hebrew: הכא נמי - פלוגתא דאחרים ורבנן, כשבססן ממש, כשנמלך לסיכוך:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:4:1.english: Here too - The dispute between Aḥerim and the Rabbis [is in a case] where he actually trampled them, when he reconsidered [their use] for roofing.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:5:1.hebrew: האי מאי - בשלמא גבי פלוגתא דר' יוסי דקא מיירי בגורן, איכא למימר טעמא דרבי יוסי: דאע"ג דבססן, חזו למיהוי ידות, וניחא ליה שיהו מחוברות באוכל כמו שהן בוססות — מרציא"ה בלע"ז:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:5:1.english: What is this? - Granted concerning the dispute of Rabbi Yosei, which deals with the threshing floor, one can state the rationale of Rabbi Yosei: that even though he trampled them, they are suitable to serve as handles, and he is pleased that they remain attached to the food as they are trampled — marcie in Old French.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:5:2.english: Since they are suitable to turn over - [To turn over] the heads of the ears of grain.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:5:3.hebrew: בעתר - על ידי הידות. עתר — פורק"א. ואלמלא הידות, אין נוחין להפכן בה, דמתוך שהם קצרים, יוצאין מבין ב' עוקציה של עתר ונשמטין ממנה. והוא כשבססן — תחלתן לא לבטלן נתכוון, אלא לרככן:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:5:3.english: With a pitchfork - By means of the handles. An atar is a fourche [pitchfork]. And were it not for the handles, it would not be convenient to turn them over with it, for since they are short, they would slip out from between the two prongs of the pitchfork and fall away from it. And this [applies] when he trampled them, [where] from the outset he did not intend to nullify them, but rather to soften them.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:6:1.english: However, here - Where he needs them for roofing [sekhakh].

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:6:2.hebrew: למאי חזו - ידות אוכלים, משבססן ואינן אגודות בהן:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:6:2.english: For what are they suited - The handles of food, once he has trampled them and they are not bundled together.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:6:3.hebrew: בגילייהו - בקשין שלהם יאחזום, וינטלו ראשי השבלים עמהם:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:6:3.english: By their straw - By their straw they will grasp them, and the heads of the ears [of grain] will be lifted with them.

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:8:1.hebrew: משום הכי מטמא רבי יוסי - דקסבר: מעשה זוטא לא בטלה תורת ידות מינייהו. שאלתי את מורי: מגופה דמשנה דמייתי אגב גררא בשמעתין, מי שייך למיתני 'גופא', כדגר' במימרות האמוראים? ואמר לי רבי: משום דהך משנה מן הטהרות, שאין מהם שום גמרא בעולם, ולא מפורשת כשאר המשניות — לפיכך נוהג הש"ס לומר 'גופא' כדי לפרש:
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:8:1.english: This is why Rabbi Yosei deems [them] ritually impure - For he holds: [Through] a minor action, the status of handles was not nullified from them. I asked my teacher: Regarding [the citation of] “the matter itself” [gufa] on a Mishnah that is brought tangentially in our sugya — is it appropriate to teach “the matter itself,” as we learn regarding the statements of the Amora’im? And my teacher said to me: Because this Mishnah is from [the Order of] Tehorot, for which there is no Gemara in the world, and it is not explained like the other Mishnayot — therefore, the Talmud is accustomed to saying “the matter itself” [gufa] in order to explain [it].

Rashi on Sukkah 14a:9:1.hebrew: למה נמשלה כו' - אגב דאמר "הואיל וראויות להפך בעתר", נקט נמי הא מלתא: "למה נמשלה כו'", דכתיב: "ויעתר (אל ה')" (בראשית כה, כא), "ויעתר לו" (שם):
Rashi on Sukkah 14a:9:1.english: Why are [the prayers of the righteous] likened, etc. - Since [the Gemara] said, “Since they are fit to be turned over with a pitchfork,” it also cited this matter: “Why are [the prayers of the righteous] likened, etc.?” As it is written: “And [Isaac] entreated [vayetar] (the Lord)” (Genesis 25:21), [and] “and [the Lord] was entreated [vaye'ater] by him” (ibid.).

Tosafot on Sukkah 14a:2:1.hebrew: כל ידות האוכלין שבססן בגורן טהורות - משנה היא פ"ק דעוקצין (מ"ה):
Tosafot on Sukkah 14a:2:1.english: "All handles of food that one besasan on the threshing floor are ritually pure" - This is a Mishnah in the first chapter of Oktzin (Mishnah 5).

Tosafot on Sukkah 14a:5:1.hebrew: בעתר - בפרק הבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף סד.) פי' בקונטרס: עתר — פל"א בלע"ז. ולא יתכן, דבלא ידות נמי יכול להפך בה את התבואה; והיא נקראת רחת, שמטהרין בה את התבואה מן המוץ שלה, כדכתיב (ישעיהו ל׳:כ״ד): "אשר זורה ברחת ובמזרה". וכאן פירש: פורק"א, וכן עיקר:
Tosafot on Sukkah 14a:5:1.english: With an eter - In the chapter [entitled] "Haba Al Yevamto" (Yevamot 64a), Rashi explained: Eter is pelle [shovel] in Old French. And [this] cannot be, for even without handles [attached stalks], one could also turn over the grain with it; and that [implement] is called a rachat [winnowing shovel], with which they cleanse the grain from its chaff, as it is written (Isaiah 30:24): "Which has been winnowed with shovel and with fork." And here [in our tractate], he explained [it as] fourche [pitchfork], and this is primary.
